engine: @opencode-ai/codemode: a tree-walking JavaScript interpreter written in JS (acorn parser, Effect fibers for async), running inside the Executor server's own Node.js process and heap. Not a V8 isolate, not workerd, not a subprocess. App tools themselves run in a separate workerd process.

defaults.time: 300,000 ms wall per execute, discovery plus program (packages/mcp/src/contracts/execute.ts:511); operator can change it with EXECUTOR_MCP_TIMEOUT_MS (apps/local/server/src/contracts/config.ts:61). Approval wait does not count (verified).
defaults.memory: none. The interpreter shares the server's Node heap (about 4 GB default on this machine); exceeding it crashes the server.
defaults.output: none. Executor passes no maxOutputBytes (packages/mcp/src/implementation/execute.ts:1784-1785); value and logs return whole (200,000-char log came back intact).

Also: 65,536-char source cap (contracts/execute.ts:32 and 243), 64 live programs per server (implementation/executions.ts:767), 2,000 nested async calls (codemode promises.js:19).

source_notes.finding: Each app tool becomes a CodeMode Tool.make with the app's input/output schemas (execute.ts:1001-1009); the program sees one global proxy, tools, a path-accumulating ToolReference (codemode interpreter/runtime.js:168). Signatures are rendered to TypeScript text only when search pages are read (codemode tool-schema.js:201, 248; patches/codemode-lazy-catalog.md).

On demand. The MCP surface is fixed: skills, search, describe, call, execute, resume. Inside a program, tools.search, tools.search.describe and a global search() are served by Executor's backend BM25 search (execute.ts:1751-1782; patches/codemode-host-search.md). Apps not named statically are lazy namespaces loaded on first use (execute.ts:1415, 1771; patches/codemode-lazy-namespaces.md).

No serialization boundary to the interpreter: a tools.* call is an Effect forked in the same process (codemode runtime.js:230), arguments copied as JSON data (tool-runtime.js:448-450), then backend.callTool sends it to the app runtime (execute.ts:973-981), which runs the app in a separate workerd process (packages/sdk/src/implementation/workerd-apps.ts:189-190, whose own comment says 'Agent execute(code) is unrelated'). Approval pause holds the program's fibers with a custom scheduler (implementation/program-scheduler.ts, executions.ts:777).

The code is TypeScript-transpiled and parsed with acorn (codemode interpreter/execute.js:89-108), then walked by an interpreter whose global scope is an explicit allowlist: tools, search, Promise, Symbol, Object, Math, JSON, Number, String, Boolean, Array, console, Date, RegExp, Map, Set, URL, URLSearchParams, URI functions, Error constructors (runtime.js:168-197). No this, globalThis, Function, eval, timers. The boundary is the interpreter's object model, not a process or isolate: it runs in the Executor server's Node process. Docs say so: 'Limits are cooperative, not process isolation' (apps/docs/content/mcp.md:120-122).

Both value (last expression or return) and console logs, plus toolCalls with per-call outcome and duration, wrapped in {status, execution, unavailableApps}. CodeMode can truncate (execute.js:86, 119-182) but Executor never sets maxOutputBytes.

Time: Effect.timeoutOrElse around the program (codemode execute.js:49-78), with Executor substituting a deadline clock so approval time is excluded (execute.ts:1651-1667). The loop is stoppable because Effect preempts a fiber every 2,048 ops; patched Turn keeps JS run-to-completion (promises.js:23-31). Tool calls: recordCall throws ToolCallLimitExceeded at calls.length >= max (tool-runtime.js:403-407), and it is a catchable program error. Source: schema maxLength on the MCP input (contracts/execute.ts:243). Memory: nothing.

Fresh per execution: a new Interpreter and scope per call (codemode execute.js:19-32). No snapshots; a program paused for approval lives only in server memory, and a restart loses it (docs mcp.md 'What is coming later'; resumeUnavailableMessage 'lost' in contracts/execute.ts).

normalizeError maps a program throw to {kind: ExecutionFailure, message: 'Uncaught: <message>'} with no stack and no location (codemode interpreter/errors.js:31-54). Interpreter-detected errors (unknown identifier, unsupported syntax, bad property) do carry {line, column}. A failing tool call becomes ToolFailure with a call_ reference (execute.ts:1884-1887).

Approval is declared per tool in app code (always()/never()); execute returns status approval-required with requestId and the exact invocation, and resume({requestId, response:{action}}) continues the same program. Verified: a 15 s approval wait under a 10 s timeout still completed. Credentials never enter the interpreter: accounts are resolved on the host and passed to the app in workerd (execute.ts:966-981). The local bearer key at plain /mcp gets model mode, because the URL parser defaults to model (packages/mcp-auth/src/contracts/grant.ts:143).

surprises: The 'sandboxed interpreter' is a JS-in-JS tree-walker running in the Executor server's own Node process. A program's memory is the server's memory: P7 crashed the whole local server with a V8 heap OOM in about 62 s and dropped every session. Docs do hedge with 'cooperative, not process isolation', but name no memory limit, and there is none.

A one-line synchronous infinite recursion, function f(n){return f(n+1)} f(0), crashed the whole server with a heap OOM in 31.5 s, twice (peak RSS 4.4 GB). Executor's own patch notes say 'Sync recursion is unchanged: it never overflows and runs until TimeoutExceeded' (patches/codemode-run-to-completion.md:85). The 5-minute timeout never gets a chance.
After the server crash a workerd child process was left orphaned (PPID 1).

The 100-call cap counts tools.search calls too: search plus 100 lookups failed. Hitting the cap is a catchable exception inside the program (a try/catch loop got 100 results and the error message), but uncaught it interrupts every in-flight call (101 parallel lookups: 100 interrupted, result failed in 30 ms).
Thrown errors keep only the message: 'Uncaught: probe-boom', with no line number or stack, even though the interpreter reports line and column for its own errors.

Common JS idioms do not exist: globalThis, this, setTimeout, Function, Object.getPrototypeOf. Docs mention no timers; the rest is undocumented and makes the P8 and P12 probe forms fail at parse or lookup time rather than at a security check.

Docs match on the rest: 65,536 chars passes and 65,537 is rejected by the MCP schema (-32602); while(true) is stopped at 300,010 ms; results come back whole; approval wait is excluded from the time budget; other executions stay responsive (8 ms) while one program spins.
